title: Korean Rice Cake Gochujang Pork Bolognese
notes: This is one of PiDGin's simplest dishes and a great example of two distinct cultures coming together to create something new … two Italian preparations turned on their head with Korean interpretations. The first is a play on gnocchi, the light and beautiful Italian potato-based pasta. Instead of gnocchi here are Korean rice cakes, a more dense, chewy rice-based preparation. The other is a play on a classic Italian Bolognese, where we use gochujung, a fermented Korean chili paste to create some heat.

ingredientSections.heading: Rice Cake Gochujang Bolognese
items: 880g cylindrical Korean rice cakes (from a Korean supermarket, find an unflavoured version. They are known as "Dok" in Korean or the Chinese version is called "Nian Gao".)

methodSections.heading: Korean Bolognese Sauce
steps: Heat up a large saucepan to high heat with a splash of canola oil. Add the ground pork and brown evenly, stirring occasionally.
When the meat is browned, strain through a sieve and reserve the fat. Set the meat aside, add the fat back into the saucepan and reduce the temperature to a medium heat.
Add the finely diced vegetables and garlic, and sweat until the onions are translucent.
Deglaze the pot with a little sake or white wine. Add the tomato paste and let cook for a few moments.
Add the meat back to the saucepan with the gochujang, remaining sake or white wine and a small bay leaf and stir.
Add about half the stock and cook until the flavours develop. This will take roughly 2 hours and the vegetables will almost dissolve if chopped finely enough. Add more stock if it starts to dry out.

methodSections.heading: Rice Cake Gochujang Bolognese
steps: Cut the rice cakes into gnocchi-sized portions, 2cm (1in) is about right.
Place them in a large pot and then add just enough water to cover them. Bring to a boil for 2 minutes.
Add the bolognese and butter then simmer until the Bolognese has reduced and thickened and rice cakes are cooked to a medium chewy yet firm texture.
